title: Subtree of Another Tree
hints: first write a helper that checks whether two trees, given their root indices, are exactly identical (same values, same shape)
subRoot doesn't have to match at root's own root - it could match starting at any node inside root
walk through every node of root, and at each one, run the identical-trees check against subRoot's root
if the identical-trees check succeeds at any node, return true immediately; if you exhaust every node of root without a match, return false
commonMistakes: only checking whether subRoot matches at root's own root, instead of trying every node of root as a potential match point
checking that subRoot's values appear somewhere in root without verifying the exact shape (missing/extra children in the wrong places)
forgetting the sentinel means a node has no left or right child, and letting a mismatch here silently pass as a match

content.problemStatement:
Binary trees in these problems are encoded as a flat array using
complete-binary-tree (heap) indexing:

- the root sits at index 0
- a node at index `i` has its left child at index `2*i+1` and right child at index `2*i+2`
- a child index only counts as real if it's within the array's bounds **and** its value isn't the sentinel `-101`
- any position at or beyond the end of the array, or holding `-101`, means "no node there" - real node values are always in the range -100 to 100, so -101 can never be mistaken for a genuine value

You're given two trees encoded this way, `root` and `subRoot`.

**Return true if subRoot's exact structure and values appear anywhere in root, rooted at some node of root, and false otherwise.**

That node and every descendant must match subRoot node for node, in the same shape. subRoot matching root's entire tree also counts as true.
constraints: every real node value in both trees is between -100 and 100 inclusive
the sentinel value -101 marks a missing node and never appears as a real value
notes: subRoot's values all appear somewhere in root, but never in matching shape (e.g. as a subtree of a subtree, or with extra/missing children)
root and subRoot both being a single node
duplicate values appearing at multiple places in root, only one of which is a true structural match

optimal.time: O(m * n) in the worst case (there is a faster O(m+n) serialization-based approach, but the direct recursive check is the expected solution here)
optimal.space: O(h1 + h2) for the recursion stack
optimal.pattern: tree DFS: recursively test every node of root as a candidate root for a same-tree comparison against subRoot

bruteForce.approach: same as optimal - for every node in root, check whether the subtree rooted there is structurally identical to subRoot
bruteForce.time: O(m * n) where n is the size of root and m is the size of subRoot, since each of the n candidate roots can trigger an O(m) comparison
bruteForce.space: O(h1 + h2) recursion stack for the two trees' heights
